# 1.1. On Model Selection With Raw Traits 
Here we will select the best model to explain each trait variation, we base this model on multiple hypothesis testing. 
# Packages 

```{r}
# Clear the environment and load required packages
rm(list = ls()) ## Empty environment
gc() # Clean up memory

# Required libraries (some are commented out for optional installation)
library(conflicted)   # Manage conflicts between packages
library(tidyverse)    # Data manipulation and visualization
library(openxlsx)     # Export results to Excel
library(vegan)        # Ecological analysis (e.g., community matrix)
library(readxl)       # Read Excel files
library(reshape)      # Data reshaping
library(reshape2)     # Alternative reshaping tools
library(SYNCSA)       # Trait-based community ecology
library(jtools)       # Model summary output formatting
library(interactions) # For interaction terms in models
library(bbmle)        # Model selection and AIC comparison

# Reproducibility settings
set.seed(811)              # Reproducible randomization
options(scipen = 999)      # Avoid scientific notation in numeric output
conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter(), dplyr::mutate()) # Prefer dplyr functions
```
# Community Matrix 
Again we load and adjust the community matrix.
```{r}
# Load species frequency data (site x species matrix)
d <- read_xlsx("data/data_ferns.xlsx", sheet = "w_matrix")

# Build a community matrix of absolute frequencies
w_matrix <- reshape2::acast(
  site ~ taxa,
  data = d,
  value.var = "FA_New",
  fun.aggregate = sum
) %>%
  round(digits = 2)

head(w_matrix) # Preview matrix
```

# X Variables 
Now, the predictors...
```{r}
x_ncor <- read_xlsx("data/data_ferns.xlsx", sheet = 'e_matrix') %>%
  dplyr::filter(Site %in% rownames(w_matrix)) |>
  column_to_rownames("Site")
```

# Trait Matrix 
Finally, the trait matrix. Here we will transform each trait to binary (presence/absence).
```{r}
#Load trait matrix
t_matrix <- read_xlsx("data/data_ferns.xlsx", sheet = 't_matrix') 
# Convert categorical trait variables into binary format (presence/absence)
rhiz_type <- table(t_matrix$taxa, t_matrix$rhizome_type)
morph <- table(t_matrix$taxa, t_matrix$frond_morphology)

# Create trait matrix: species x traits (binary + numeric)
t <- cbind.data.frame(
  diam = t_matrix[order(t_matrix$taxa), ]$rhizome_diameter,
  r_comp = rhiz_type[order(rownames(rhiz_type)), "Compact"],
  r_cr = rhiz_type[order(rownames(rhiz_type)), "Short-Creeping"],
  r_lr = rhiz_type[order(rownames(rhiz_type)), "Long-Creeping"],
  lmseg = t_matrix[order(order(t_matrix$taxa)), ]$laminae_dissection,
  ltri = t_matrix[order(t_matrix$taxa), ]$laminae_pubescence,
  buds = t_matrix[order(t_matrix$taxa), ]$proliferous_buds,
  ind = t_matrix[order(t_matrix$taxa), ]$indusium,
  ldim = morph[order(rownames(morph)), 'Dimorphic'],
  chl = t_matrix[order(order(t_matrix$taxa)), ]$spore_chlorophyll
) %>%
  filter(rownames(.) %in% colnames(w_matrix))

# Inspect resulting trait matrix
dim(t)
head(t)
glimpse(t)
view(t)
```

# Organizing the raw dataset 

```{r}
trait_raw <- organize.syncsa(
  w_matrix,
  traits = t,
  envir = x_ncor
)
identical(rownames(trait_raw$traits), colnames(trait_raw$community))
```

# Compute CWM
Now we will compute the community weighted mean for each trait, but using absolute frequency as weight.

```{r}
cwm_values <- matrix.t(trait_raw$community, trait_raw$traits)$matrix.T %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column('Site') %>%
  add_column(trait_raw$environmental)
```

# Model selection
Now we will select the best model for each trait, as following:
1) Creating a list of models names (see Appendix S1 for the hypothesis of each model);
2) Elaborating the linear models, based on the list;
3) Select the most parsimonious models based on AICc;
4) Filter only the best model (dAICc = 0);
5) Save in a new object for summarize in a table.

## Rhizome diameter 

```{r}

# Create list of candidate models to explain this trait 
models <- c(
  "diam ~ max_temp, data = cwm_values",
  "diam ~ max_temp + ann_prec,data = cwm_values",
  "diam ~ ann_prec*prec_seas",
  "diam ~ nitrogen, data =cwm_values",
  "diam ~ cec, data = cwm_values",
  "diam ~ nitrogen + cec, data = cwm_values",
  "diam ~ 1"
)

# Fit linear models
md1 <- lm(diam ~ max_temp_wam + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)

md2 <- lm(
  diam ~ max_temp_wam + ann_prec + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = cwm_values
)

md3 <- lm(
  diam ~ ann_prec * prec_seas + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = cwm_values
)

md4 <- lm(diam ~ nitrogen + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)

md5 <- lm(diam ~ cec + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)

md6 <- lm(diam ~ nitrogen + cec + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)

md7 <- lm(diam ~ 1 + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)


# Select the best model 
sel_md <- AICctab(
  md1,
  md2,
  md3,
  md4,
  md5,
  md6,
  md7,
  base = T,
  delta = T,
  mnames = models
)
class(sel_md) <- "data.frame" #insert class at ictab
sel_md

# Filter the best model
result_diam <- cbind.data.frame(
  models = rownames(sel_md),
  sel_md,
  row.names = NULL
) %>%
  filter(dAICc == 0)

mod_diam <- md3
summary(md3, digits = 3)
```
## Rhyzome compact 

```{r}

models <- c(
  "r_comp ~ ann_prec, data = cwm_values",
  "r_comp ~ prec_seas, data = cwm_values",

  "r_comp  ~ cec, data = cwm_values",
  "r_comp  ~ nitrogen + cec, data = cwm_values",
  "r_comp  ~ 1"
)

# Fit models
md1 <- lm(r_comp ~ ann_prec + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)

md2 <- lm(
  r_comp ~ prec_seas + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = cwm_values
)

md3 <- lm(
  r_comp ~ ann_prec + prec_seas + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = cwm_values
)

md4 <- lm(
  r_comp ~ ann_prec * prec_seas + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = cwm_values
)

md5 <- lm(r_comp ~ nitrogen + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)

md6 <- lm(r_comp ~ cec + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)

md7 <- lm(
  r_comp ~ nitrogen + cec + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = cwm_values
)

md8 <- lm(r_comp ~ 1 + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)

# Select models based on AICc
sel_md <- AICctab(
  md1,
  md2,
  md3,
  md4,
  md5,
  md6,
  md7,
  md8,
  base = T,
  delta = T,
  mnames = models
)

class(sel_md) <- "data.frame" #insert class at ictab

sel_md

# Filter the best model
result_rcomp <- cbind.data.frame(
  models = rownames(sel_md),
  sel_md,
  row.names = NULL
) %>%
  filter(dAICc == 0)


mod_rcomp <- md5 # Save model
summary(md5) # Check summary
```

## Spore chlorophyll

Spore chlorophyll has shorter life span than chlorophyll, but they are able to reach long-distance before germinate. 
The shorter lifespan require more to the species reach it optimum habitat faster, therefore, with less environmental variation precipitation and soil rich.


```{r}
models <- c(
  "chl ~ ann_prec, data = cwm_values",
  "chl ~ prec_seas, data = cwm_values",
  "chl ~ max_temp_wam, data = cwm_values",
  "chl ~ prec_seas + ann_prec, data = cwm_values",
  "chl ~ ann_prec*prec_seas, data = cwm_values",
  "chl ~ max_temp_wam + ann_prec, data = cwm_values",
  "chl ~ max_temp_wam + prec_seas, data = cwm_values",
  "chl ~ clay",
  "chl ~ 1"
)

md1 <- lm(chl ~ ann_prec + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)
md2 <- lm(chl ~ prec_seas + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)
md3 <- lm(chl ~ max_temp_wam + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)
md4 <- lm(chl ~ prec_seas + ann_prec + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)
md5 <- lm(chl ~ ann_prec * prec_seas + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)
md6 <- lm(
  chl ~ max_temp_wam + ann_prec + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = cwm_values
)
md7 <- lm(
  chl ~ max_temp_wam + prec_seas + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = cwm_values
)
md8 <- lm(chl ~ clay + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)
md9 <- lm(chl ~ 1 + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)

sel_md <- AICctab(
  md1,
  md2,
  md3,
  md4,
  md5,
  md6,
  md7,
  md8,
  md9,
  base = T,
  delta = T,
  mnames = models
)

class(sel_md) <- "data.frame" #insert class at ictab

sel_md

result_chl <- cbind.data.frame(
  models = rownames(sel_md),
  sel_md,
  row.names = NULL
) %>%
  filter(., dAICc == 0)
summary(md5)

mod_chl <- md5
```
# Output

```{r}
# Export all best models to an Excel file using jtools
jtools::export_summs(
  mod_diam,
  mod_lr,
  mod_rcr,
  mod_rcomp,
  mod_lmseg,
  mod_ltri,
  mod_buds,
  mod_ind,
  mod_ldim,
  mod_chl,
  model.names = c(
    "Rhiz. Diameter",
    "Rhiz. Long-Creeping",
    "Rhiz. Short-Creeping",
    "Rhiz. Compact",
    "Lam. Multi-Seg",
    "Lam. Pubescent",
    "Proliferous buds",
    "Indusium",
    "Lam. Dimorphism",
    "Spore Chlorophyll"
  ),
  digits = 3,
  coefs = c(
    "Intercept" = "(Intercept)",
    "Soil's Nitrogen" = "nitrogen",
    "Annual Rainfall" = "ann_prec",
    "Rainfall Seasonallity" = "prec_seas",
    "Annual Rainfall:Rainfall Seasonallity" = "ann_prec:prec_seas",
    "Plot Size" = "plot_size",
    "Sample Effort" = "samp_size"
  ),
  #faster way to save models data
  statistics = c(
    R2 = "r.squared",
    Fstatistic = {
      'statistic'
    },
    "AIC",
    "df"
  ),
  error_format = "p = {p.value}",
  bold_signif = 0.05,
  to.file = "xlsx",
  file.name = "outputs/cwm_raw.xlsx"
)


# Save all selected models to disk
 mod_list <-list(mod_diam,
  mod_lr,
  mod_rcr,
  mod_rcomp,
  mod_lmseg,
  mod_ltri,
  mod_buds,
  mod_ind,
  mod_ldim,
  mod_chl)

saveRDS(mod_list, file = 'outputs/list_raw_cwm_models.RDS')

#Creating data.frame for all results
forw <- rbind(
  result_diam,
  result_rcomp,
  result_crep,
  result_lr,
  result_lmseg,
  result_ltri,
  result_buds,
  result_ind,
  result_lmor,
  result_chl
) %>%
  mutate(
    trait = c(
      rep("rdiam", length(grep("diam", .$models))),
      rep("r_comp", length(grep("comp", .$models))),
      rep("r_crep", length(grep("cr", .$models))),
      rep("r_lr", length(grep("lr", .$models))),
      rep("lam_seg", length(grep("lseg", .$models))),
      rep("lam_mseg", length(grep("mseg", .$models))),
      rep("tric_lam", length(grep("ltri", .$models))),
      rep("buds", length(grep("buds", .$models))),
      rep("indus", length(grep("ind", .$models))),
      rep("lam_morf", length(grep("ldim", .$models))),
      rep("chl", length(grep("chl", .$models)))
    ),
    .before = AICc
  )

forw

# Changing models names to predictors names only
result <- gsub("cwm_values.*~ ", "", forw$models) %>%
  gsub("x_ncor\\$", "", .) %>%
  gsub(", data.*", "", .) %>%
  mutate(dplyr::select(forw, -models), predictors = ., .before = AICc)

# Separating good from bad models
rows <- grep("1", result$predictors)
nice_mods <- result[-rows, ]
bad_mods <- result[rows, ]

dim(nice_mods) # 5 nice_mods
```
# Save data 

```{r}
write.xlsx(
  x = list(cwm_values, result, nice_mods, bad_mods),
  file = 'outputs/cwm_raw_results.xlsx',
  rowNames = T,
  overwrite = T
)

saveRDS(cwm_values, file = "data/cwm_values_raw.RDS")
cwm_values <- readRDS("data/cwm_values_raw.RDS")
```
